questions.problem: The radius of the base of a cylinder is $3\,\text{ft}$ and its height is $4\,\text{ft}.$ Find the lateral surface area of the cylinder.
questions.worked_solution:
We can calculate the lateral surface area of a cylinder using the formula

$$
{S}_{L}=2\pi rh,
$$

where $r$ is the radius and $h$ is the height of the cylinder.

Substituting $r=3\,\text{ft}$ and $h=4\,\text{ft}$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{L} & =2\pi (3)(4)=24\pi \,{\text{ft}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: The lateral surface area of a cylinder is $864\pi \,{\text{cm}}^{2}$ and the ratio of its height to its radius is $3.$ Calculate the radius of the cylinder.
questions.worked_solution:
Let $r$ and $h$ be the radius and height of the cylinder, respectively. 

We are given that 

$$
\frac{h}{r}=3\,⟹\,h=3r.
$$

We can find the lateral surface area of a cylinder using the formula

$$
{S}_{L}=2\pi rh.
$$

Substituting the values

$$
{S}_{L}=864\pi ,\,h=3r
$$

into the formula for ${S}_{L},$ we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{L} & =2\pi rh \\ 864\pi  & =2\pi r(3r) \\ 864\pi  & =6\pi {r}^{2} \\ {r}^{2} & =\frac{864\pi }{6\pi } \\ {r}^{2} & =144 \\ r & =12\,\text{cm}\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we disregard the negative solution since length must be positive.

questions.problem: The surface area of a cylinder is $24\pi \,{\text{mm}}^{2}$ and the ratio of its radius to its height is $3.$ Calculate the height of the cylinder.
questions.worked_solution:
Let $r$ and $h$ be the radius and height of the cylinder, respectively. 

We are given that 

$$
\frac{r}{h}=3\,⟹\,r=3h.
$$

We can find the surface area of a cylinder using the formula

$$
S=2\pi {r}^{2}+2\pi rh.
$$

Substituting the values

$$
S=24\pi ,\,r=3h
$$

into the formula for $S,$ we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =2\pi {r}^{2}+2\pi rh \\ 24\pi  & =2\pi (3h)^{2}+2\pi (3h)h \\ 24\pi  & =18\pi {h}^{2}+6\pi {h}^{2} \\ 24\pi  & =24\pi {h}^{2} \\ {h}^{2} & =\frac{24\pi }{24\pi } \\ {h}^{2} & =1 \\ h & =1\,\text{mm}\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we disregard the negative solution since length must be positive.

Example: 
                    Finding a Dimension of a Cylinder Given Its Surface Area or Lateral Surface Area
canonical_examples.problem: The lateral surface area of a cylinder is $900\pi \: \textrm{in}^2$ and the ratio of its height to its radius is $2.$ Calculate the radius of the cylinder.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Let $r$ and $h$ be the radius and height of the cylinder, respectively. 

We are given that 

$$
\dfrac{h}{r}=2
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
h=2r.
$$

We can find the lateral surface area of a cylinder using the formula

$$
S_L =  2\pi rh.
$$

Substituting the values

$$
S_L=900\pi, \qquad h=2r
$$

into the formula for $S_L,$ we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{L} & =2\pi rh \\ 900\pi  & =2\pi r(2r) \\ 900\pi  & =4\pi {r}^{2} \\ {r}^{2} & =\frac{900\pi }{4\pi } \\ {r}^{2} & =225 \\ r & =15\,\text{in}\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we disregard the negative solution since length must be positive.

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
A cylinder's **lateral surface area** is the surface area that does not include the bases. 

Suppose we want to calculate the lateral surface area of the right cylinder shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14268062/assets/77a6f3e455661baf2fcfdc820b8e5b9f5b0aeadf68c3575d5dc3b59b34a768cc.png)

Since we're considering only the lateral surface area, let's assume that the cylinder has no bases (i.e., no top or bottom). 

Now, imagine cutting the cylinder along a vertical line and "unfolding" the lateral part. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14268062/assets/a6c160796c52154395986b340cb09f5146f8a957660cca67777a79bd3feff008.png)

Doing this, we get a rectangle, as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14268062/assets/132a444c73521ec69f5d27fd0e1b13f8b0f280e21f7e3b402d8655295f71c613.png)

Notice the following:

- the length of our rectangle is $2\pi r$ since it must be equal to the circumference of the bases

- the height of our rectangle is $h$

Therefore, the area of the rectangle, and thus the cylinder's lateral surface area $S_L$, is given by

$$
S_L = 2\pi r\cdot  h = 2\pi r h.
$$

For example, if the radius of a cylinder is $r=3 \,\textrm{cm}$ and its height is $h=5\,\textrm{cm},$ the lateral surface area will be

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{L} & =2\pi (3)(5)=30\pi \,{\text{cm}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

tutorials.name: Deriving the Formula for the Full Surface Area of a Cylinder
tutorials.problem:
We now wish to find a formula for the total surface area of a right cylinder. To do this, let's consider a right cylinder of radius $r$ and height $h,$ as shown below. This time, we include the bases.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14268062/assets/d3320f15008796a4c49366ebe7f0933ac7d018aeefb212adca59fd134e656d3d.png)

The net of the cylinder is constructed from the lateral surface plus two congruent circular bases.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14268062/assets/02365f72f440f99f51d290c775017be62582be5742f0c3dfde0b545465b94754.png)

Let $S_L$ be the lateral surface area of the cylinder, and let $S_B$ be the area of the bases. The surface area $S$ of the cylinder can be expressed

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =2{S}_{B}+{S}_{L} \\  & =2(\pi {r}^{2})+2\pi r\cdot h \\  & =2\pi {r}^{2}+2\pi rh.\end{aligned}
$$
